tip: Use RPE to auto-regulate daily training.
actionable_advice: An RPE 8 means leaving 2 reps in reserve. Adjust weight based on daily fatigue.
Rotate heavy/intensity, light/speed, and medium/hypertrophy days within the same week.
Cue your foot placement, grip, and bracing exactly the same way every set.
Drop total training volume by 30–50% to clear accumulated CNS fatigue.
Breathe deep into your belly, expand your obliques against your belt, and brace.
If you add weight to the bar, keep sets and reps identical to last week.
Program paused benches for weakness off the chest, or board presses for lockout issues.
Aim for 7–9 hours nightly to maximise growth hormone release and tissue repair.
Drive heels down to push your torso up the bench without lifting your glutes.

tip: Transition smoothly from hypertrophy to peaking.
actionable_advice: Gradually drop reps (from 8–10 down to 1–3) while increasing intensity over 6–12 weeks.
Move the empty barbell with the same speed and intent as a 90% 1RM attempt.
Stop a strength set if bar speed drops by more than 10–20%.

tip: Pull the slack out of the deadlift bar.
actionable_advice: Listen for the barbell 'click', wedge your hips, and pull with 50% tension before lifting.
Consume 500–1000mg of sodium and 20 oz of water 90 minutes before lifting.
Hold a 1-second count at the bottom of the lift to eliminate momentum.
Match every set of heavy pressing with a set of rows or face pulls.

tip: Maintain a neutral neck in the squat.
actionable_advice: Fix your eyes on the floor 4–6 feet ahead instead of looking up at a mirror.
Practice your peak singles using formal commands (Squat, Bench, Rack).
Separate training into distinct phases: accumulation (volume), transmutation (strength), and realization (taper).

tip: Use active recovery on rest days.
actionable_advice: Do 20–30 minutes of low-intensity walking or cycling to flush metabolic waste.
